solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go via Rye, opening trivial charge

parts.note: go in the sense of energy or vim is pep
via, meaning by way of, is per
rye is a cereal crop, a kind of corn
an opening such as a tear in cloth is a rent

explanation.surface: Someone taking a route through Rye in Sussex finds a small fee charged at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Every clue word reads as travel directions, but each is a synonym: Rye is the grain, not the Sussex town.
explanation.definitionFit: A token payment of a single peppercorn was historically used as a nominal, almost trivial, charge for a lease.

clue.text: Dreyfus planned new magazines

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a fresh arrangement, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Alfred Dreyfus, the French officer of the famous affair, plans some fresh periodicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective for the magazines but is the anagram signal for DREYFUS PLANNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap sensational Victorian periodicals were sold as serial publications, so they were magazines of a lurid kind.

clue.text: Nothing less than compensation he'll set for secret police

indicators.note: set means arranged or put in order, signalling that the letters are rearranged
less than means minus, so the letter for nothing is taken away from the following word

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone claims that nothing short of financial redress will do, before turning to the subject of secret police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' removes one O from COMPENSATION; the remaining letters plus HE'LL are rearranged by 'set'.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives working out of uniform, in civilian dress, are effectively undercover or secret police.

clue.text: Oath exemplified by commercial

parts.note: exemplified, as in for example, is e.g.
a commercial is an advert, an ad

explanation.surface: A swear word turns up in a television advertisement as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned mild exclamation or minced oath, a softened form of 'by God'.

clue.text: Presides over church broadcasts

parts.note: to broadcast a programme is to air it, so broadcasts are airs

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of a church also puts out its radio services.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside over a meeting is to run it from the top seat, the role of its head.

clue.text: Unstable lira used in payment to film actor

indicators.note: unstable means not fixed in place, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A shaky Italian currency is used to pay a movie star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unstable' looks like a comment on the old Italian currency but signals an anagram of LIRA USED.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalty-style fee paid to performers each time a film or show is repeated.

clue.text: Classified course note receiving degree

parts.note: a course of treatment or diet is a regimen
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A graded course note is handed back with a degree mark on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regimented has been organised into strict classes or groups, so it has been classified.

clue.text: You'll need it to win the Dunmow flitch and certainly not this?

definitions.text: You'll need it to win the Dunmow flitch
definitions.meaning: the Dunmow Flitch is an Essex custom awarding a side of bacon to a married couple who have not quarrelled for a year and a day
read as 'never a' plus the kind of puzzle being solved, a jokey denial of what this grid is

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek remark about an old Essex bacon prize and the puzzle in front of you.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dunmow Flitch is a traditional prize from Great Dunmow in Essex, England, for a couple with a year of marital harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: A year without a single quarrel is required, and split differently the phrase also denies being a word puzzle.

clue.text: Clydeside sales talk with name for fabric

parts.note: Paisley is a Scottish town in the Clydeside conurbation west of Glasgow
patter is a salesman's glib talk

explanation.surface: A Glasgow-area salesman's spiel, with a brand name, sells a type of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirling teardrop design originating in the Scottish weaving town, used on printed cloth.

clue.text: On the way back, once more, some rain falls

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling in reverse, so the word that follows is read right to left

parts.note: once more means again

indicators.note: some means only part of the word rain is kept, its tail dropped

explanation.surface: Heading home, the traveller is caught in yet another downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border, so the name can stand for the falls themselves.

clue.text: Southern Spain — travel through Spanish city

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south or southern
E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain (España)
to travel is to go
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: A traveller heads through the south of Spain on the way to a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic city north-west of Madrid, famous for its Roman aqueduct, so it is a Spanish city.

clue.text: Haul made by New Yorker?

definitions.meaning: to haul is to pull sharply, to jerk
a slang name for an American, especially a Northerner; the baseball team of New York is the Yankees

explanation.surface: A catch landed by someone from New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp pull is a jerk or tug, and Americans, New Yorkers above all, are nicknamed this way.

clue.text: Winds pick up vessel headed by master making peculiar signs

indicators.note: pick up means take on board, so the winds hold the other letters inside

parts.note: the trades are the trade winds

indicators.note: headed by means the master letter comes in front of the vessel

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree
Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: Breezes lift a boat captained by a skipper, producing strange signals.
explanation.walkthrough: Trade winds are the steady winds of the tropics, shortened to 'the trades'.
explanation.definitionFit: A registered logo or name is a distinctive sign peculiar to one maker's goods.

clue.text: Short distance in borders of Timor — two miles off, about

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the edges of Timor
off means awry or wrong, signalling that the letters are rearranged
two means the word for miles is written down twice

parts.note: a mile is a unit of distance; the plural asks for more than one

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outside letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: A traveller is a small way inside the Timor frontier, roughly two miles out of position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges MILEMILE into MILLIMEE, and 'about' wraps that round TR, the borders of Timor.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousandth of a metre is a tiny unit of length, a short distance.

clue.text: Arrive mob-handed — getting very drunk, almost

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: rolling drunk means extremely drunk

explanation.surface: A gang turns up in force, having had far too much to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive in large numbers is idiomatically to come pouring or flooding in, as a crowd does.

clue.text: It's not easy to shake off this goose?

definitions.text: It's not easy to shake off this goose?

parts.words: It's not easy to shake off this goose?
parts.note: a shellfish that clings to rocks and hulls shares its name with a species of goose, so this goose is hard to get rid of

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a bird you cannot get away from.
explanation.definitionFit: The crustacean clings stubbornly, and a black-and-white goose of the Arctic bears the same name.

clue.text: Given higher award — possibly DD (Prague)

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone receives a better honour, perhaps a Doctor of Divinity from Prague.
explanation.walkthrough: DD looks like the Doctor of Divinity degree, fitting 'award', but its letters join PRAGUE as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be raised to a better grade is to receive a higher rank or mark.

clue.text: African runner's bounding run by stake

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: an ante is a poker player's stake
a lope is a long bounding stride

explanation.surface: A sprinter leaps along past a fence post.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift hoofed animal of the African plains is a fast runner.

clue.text: Make good press following wreck being discovered

indicators.note: following means the press comes after the trimmed wreck
discovered means uncovered, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: Reporters arrive after a shipwreck is found.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover losses is to make them good, compensating for what was spent.

clue.text: Whither Einstein? The answer's there

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the solution sits there, inside the preceding words

explanation.surface: A question about where the great physicist went, with the reply that it is right there.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in this place or document, which is just where the clue says the solution lies.

clue.text: Quick to accept one old coin for collectors' fair

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the quick word holds the others

parts.note: fleet means fast or quick
one can be the indefinite article a
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Collectors at a fair are quick to take an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A street market of second-hand goods and curios is a favourite haunt for collectors.

clue.text: It will attract attention from posh set's regulars

indicators.note: regulars here means letters taken at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Something catches the eye of the smart crowd's frequent visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulars' looks like habitual patrons of a posh set's haunt, but it picks the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A whispered hiss used to catch someone's notice quietly.

clue.text: Singular trousers, apparently, for Jacob's son

indicators.note: singular means in the one-only form, so the plural S is dropped

parts.note: Levis are a brand of jeans

explanation.surface: A single pair of trousers, seemingly, belongs to a biblical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' admits the joke: trousers have no true singular, but one 'Levi' looks like it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch Jacob had twelve sons; the third, by Leah, founded the priestly tribe.

clue.text: Restricted cover hides very little

indicators.note: hides means conceals within, so the cover holds the next piece

parts.note: a lid is a cover
a mite is a very small amount

explanation.surface: A tight cover conceals almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept within limits or confined is restricted in scope or number.

clue.text: Sight the compiler viewed, he said

indicators.note: he said means the words are spoken, so we want what they sound like

parts.note: the compiler refers to himself as I, and viewed is saw

explanation.surface: The setter reports what he looked at.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'I saw' and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly can be called a sight, as in 'you look a sight'.

clue.text: Capital thoroughfare where 'orse has nothing to show, returning between haunts

parts.note: a hunter is a horse; with the H dropped, cockney-style, 'orse goes with 'unter

indicators.note: between means the next piece sits inside the pair of haunts

parts.note: a den is a haunt, and the plural gives two of them

indicators.note: returning means the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing, a score with nothing to show

explanation.surface: A street where a horse has had no success, heading back between its usual haunts.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'orse signals the dropped H, so the horse is a hunter minus H. 'returning' turns NIL into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous boulevard in Berlin, Germany's capital, is a major street of that city.
